Final NWS observations and any late-day model updates will determine resolution.

The modest 11 % probability on 24 °C and very low odds above 27 °C therefore reflect the limited upside risk once the typical afternoon convection begins. Updated model runs and official observations through the morning of the 14th will be the key data releases that could still nudge the final recorded high within the narrow 24–26 °C band favored by the market.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent southwest monsoon (habagat) conditions, with scattered rains, thunderstorms, and extensive cloud cover, are the dominant factor capping Manila's daytime heating ahead of August 16. PAGASA forecasts show a 26–29°C or 26–33°C range for Metro Manila that day, reflecting reduced solar insolation from monsoon-driven convection typical of peak rainy season. Recent model consensus and ongoing low-pressure influences reinforce this moderation, keeping extremes near or below the long-term August average high of ~30–31°C. Trader sentiment clusters on 29–30°C because clearer breaks or stronger subsidence would be needed to push maxima to 31°C or higher, while heavy rain could suppress them further toward 28°C. Updated NHC/PAGASA briefings and next model runs will refine these probabilities as the short-term forecast window narrows.
